# Source and Method

This report traces the selected workspace source, [gmacsbase.TPL:L1](gmacsbase.TPL#L1), not generated C++ or a runtime log. It indexes all 80 ADMB `FUNCTION` definitions and the literal C++ helper definitions in `DATA_SECTION` and `GLOBALS_SECTION`. The exact full signature (including multiline parameters) is linked at each definition's start; the body boundary is linked separately. `FUNCTION` bodies are treated as class methods emitted by ADMB, not as part of the preceding section.

Section roots are grouped by execution role, not textual order. `DATA_SECTION` and `PARAMETER_SECTION` execute during construction; `PRELIMINARY_CALCS_SECTION` and phase hooks are separate; ADMB may re-enter `PROCEDURE_SECTION` for parameter/phase evaluations; reporting and finalization may invoke output routines again. Branches below are alternatives. Loop bodies are shown once with their bounds. Exact iteration counts and selected branches depend on inputs, flags, optimizer/phase behavior, and execution.

Only calls resolving to definitions in this TPL are expanded. Call-site links and definition links are distinct. Standard/ADMB/library, virtual selectivity-class, macro-expanded, and other-template calls are terminal external calls unless their target is established here. Sibling expression evaluation order is not inferred where C++ does not specify it.

# Recursion Summary

No direct or indirect recursive call cycle was identified among selected-file function definitions. The `CreateOutput` call from `calc_predicted_composition` is reached only from its exceptional NaN branch and is followed by `exit(-1)`; `CreateOutput` does not call back into `calc_predicted_composition`. Repeated procedure/phase evaluations and the bounded equilibrium/projection loops are repetition, not recursion.

# Coverage and Uncertainty

All 80 indexed ADMB definitions are accounted for in the execution trees or `Other Defined Functions`; function overloads are distinguished above, and repeated call sites remain separate. The seven `Subst` methods and six literal global C++ helper functions are also indexed at their definition links. There are no TPL conditional-compilation directives affecting these bodies; the global includes and `isWindows` implementation have OS-specific guards.

Unresolved/nonexpanded targets include ADMB and standard-library calls, selectivity-class virtual methods, `calc_equilibrium`, `CalcStateTAC`, `MyOutput`, and the external management executable. `calc_equilibrium`, `CalcStateTAC`, and `MyOutput` are not defined in the selected TPL; they may be supplied by included or companion templates, but generated-code correspondence was not used to attribute them. The local `dnorm` overloads are expanded only where argument types identify them; the three-argument call in `get_prior_pdf` remains an external overload-resolution uncertainty. Macro calls such as `ECHO`, `REPVEC`, and `REPMAT` are treated as output insertions, not hidden selected-file functions. No model inputs or execution were used, so branches, phase counts, and loop iteration totals are not measured.
